headline: Class 10 Student Starts Charging Peers 'Hourly Consultancy Fee' To Facilitate Offline Interactions
body:
Fourteen-year-old Kabir Sharma has emerged as the city’s leading expert in physical social navigation, charging his classmates a flat rate of ₹200 per hour to help them navigate the terrifying, real-time chaos of a school hallway without their smartphones. The initiative, which Sharma calls ‘Unplugged Facilitation,’ involves teaching peers how to maintain eye contact for more than three seconds and how to identify a ‘friend’ in the cafeteria without checking their Instagram tagged photos.

“Most of my clients have reached a stage where they experience mild hives if they aren't looking at a screen for more than five minutes,” said Sharma, who currently manages a portfolio of 12 students between his math and history periods. “Yesterday, I had to physically restrain a client from ‘double-tapping’ the cafeteria salad bar because he thought it would make the sprouts appear in his own kitchen. I’m not just charging for my time; I’m charging for the psychological trauma of teaching them how to use a physical pen.”

School administration has remained neutral on the enterprise, with one guidance counselor noting that it is the first time students have been seen talking to each other without a shared Wi-Fi connection in over three years. Meanwhile, parents have expressed mixed feelings about the billable hours. “It’s expensive, yes,” said one parent. “But seeing my son actually describe his day out loud instead of sending me a meme link via DM feels like money well spent.”

Sharma, however, has already begun planning his exit strategy, noting that the market for offline human interaction is reaching saturation. He is reportedly looking into launching a premium tier service for parents that includes a ‘Non-Digital Summer Vacation,’ where he promises to physically throw all handheld devices into a local pond while reciting stories from the 90s.
caption: Local student becomes an unlikely consultant for digital detoxing. Parents are divided, but the hallways have never been louder. #DigitalDetox #GenZ #SchoolLife #OfflineLiving (satire)
igHook: Would you pay a teenager to take your phone away for an hour?
imagePrompt: A blurry, candid shot of students in a high school corridor standing in small groups, looking awkward and glancing around at each other without any devices in their hands.

sourceHeadline.title: PM Modi urges teachers to address excessive screen time, drug addiction among students

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 creates a genuinely funny, specific premise that observes a social phenomenon (digital addiction) through a fresh, human-centric lens rather than just having a teacher do something absurd. The 'consultancy fee' idea feels like a real, slightly pathetic, and charmingly ambitious teenage invention, avoiding the trope of the teacher as the sole source of the joke.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional, archetypal name ('Kabir Sharma') to frame a satirical commentary on digital dependency among teenagers. It does not target any specific real private individual, public figure, or protected group, and the image prompt is appropriately generic.
